# Draft:King Spud Trophy

The King Spud Trophy is a college basketball rivalry trophy presented to the winner of the Idaho-Idaho State basketball series.
The trophy was originally created in the 1960's and awarded to the winning team in the schools' men's basketball series. Sometime in the early 1980's the trophy was lost, and neither Idaho nor Idaho State have been able to locate the trophy despite several attempts at searching for it.
In 2021, the University of Idaho library created a hand-sculpted model of the trophy based off of old photographs. This new model became the reference point for future reproductions of the trophy.
In 2022, students at the University of Idaho and Idaho State University approved funding to create a 3D printed replica of the trophy, with intention of the schools playing for it once again. This time the trophy would be competed for by both men's and women's basketball in a four game contest each season with point totals as a tiebreaker.
The reproduction was complete in time for the 2022 basketball season. Since it's reintroduction, Idaho State has claimed the trophy for three consecutive years.
